report_name: APT36 Linked to 'PATCHCORD' Espionage Campaign in South Asia

threat_actors.name: APT36
threat_actors.description: A threat actor aligned with Pakistani interests, attributed with moderate confidence to a cyber-espionage campaign targeting South Asia. The group uses custom backdoors PATCHCORD and SHEETCORD.
threat_actors.goals: To gather sensitive political, military, and economic intelligence from high-value entities in South Asia.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The malware was delivered via malicious files disguised as legitimate software, such as a fake VPN installer for Afghan Telecom (AFTEL).

attack_patterns.name: Shortcut Modification
attack_patterns.description: The malware establishes persistence on the host by hijacking browser shortcuts to ensure it is re-executed regularly.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The SHEETCORD malware variant uses legitimate public cloud services, specifically Google Sheets for command retrieval and GitHub Gists for data exfiltration, to conduct C2 communications and evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: System Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The malware suite has the capability to fingerprint the host system to gather information.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Command Shell
attack_patterns.description: The malware is capable of executing arbitrary commands received from the C2 channel.

malware.name: PATCHCORD
malware.description: A custom C/C++ backdoor used by APT36 in an espionage campaign. It establishes persistence, fingerprints the host, and executes remote commands.

malware.name: SHEETCORD
malware.description: A sophisticated Go-based implant and variant of PATCHCORD used by APT36. It abuses legitimate public cloud services like Google Sheets for C2 command retrieval and GitHub Gists for data exfiltration.

campaigns.name: PATCHCORD Campaign
campaigns.description: A cyber-espionage campaign attributed to APT36, active since at least March 2026. It targets telecommunications, government, and critical infrastructure in South Asia using the PATCHCORD and SHEETCORD backdoors.

identities.name: Afghan Telecom
identities.description: An Afghan telecom company whose legitimate VPN installer software was impersonated as a social engineering lure to deliver malware.

identities.name: Indian Government Entities
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the PATCHCORD espionage campaign in India.

identities.name: Indian Critical Infrastructure
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the PATCHCORD espionage campaign in India.

identities.name: Afghan Telecommunications Providers
identities.description: A class of victims targeted by the PATCHCORD espionage campaign in Afghanistan.

infrastructure.name: Google Sheets C2 Channel
infrastructure.description: The SHEETCORD malware uses a public Google Sheet to retrieve encoded commands from its operators, blending its C2 traffic with legitimate web services.

infrastructure.name: GitHub Gists Exfiltration Channel
infrastructure.description: The SHEETCORD malware uses GitHub Gists to upload and exfiltrate stolen data, blending its exfiltration traffic with legitimate developer activity.

indicators.name: Suspicious Google Sheets Access for C2
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Google Sheets Access for C2
id: 2b8c9d1e-0f3a-4b1e-8c9d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
status: experimental
description: 'Detects non-browser processes making repeated connections to Google Sheets URLs, which could indicate C2 activity similar to the SHEETCORD malware.'
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197266/intelligence/apt36-suspected-in-patchcord-espionage-campaign-using-google-sheets-c2.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.command_and_control
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host|endswith: 'docs.google.com'
    c-uri|contains: '/spreadsheets/d/'
  filter:
    c-useragent|contains:
      - 'Mozilla/'
      - 'Chrome/'
      - 'Safari/'
      - 'Edge/'
      - 'Firefox/'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects non-browser processes making repeated connections to Google Sheets, a TTP used by the SHEETCORD malware for C2.

indicators.name: Anomalous GitHub Gist API for Exfiltration
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous GitHub Gist API for Exfiltration
id: 3c9d1e2f-1a4b-4c2f-9d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e
status: experimental
description: 'Detects anomalous processes making POST requests to the GitHub Gists API, which could be a sign of data exfiltration as used by SHEETCORD malware.'
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197266/intelligence/apt36-suspected-in-patchcord-espionage-campaign-using-google-sheets-c2.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-host: 'api.github.com'
    c-uri: '/gists'
    cs-method: 'POST'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - 'git.exe'
      - 'gh.exe'
      - 'Code.exe'
      - 'curl.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects unusual processes making API calls to create or update GitHub Gists, a potential sign of data exfiltration used by SHEETCORD.

indicators.name: PATCHCORD Campaign Lure Filename
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: PATCHCORD Campaign Lure Filename
id: 4d1e2f3a-2b5c-4d3f-ad2e-3f4a5b6c7d8f
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the presence of a file named AFTEL-VPN.exe, which was used as a lure in the PATCHCORD campaign.'
references:
  - https://securityaffairs.com/197266/intelligence/apt36-suspected-in-patchcord-espionage-campaign-using-google-sheets-c2.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\AFTEL-VPN.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation or execution of the malicious lure file 'AFTEL-VPN.exe' used in the PATCHCORD campaign.
